grammarTopics.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Dua tense, dua cara melihat waktu
Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah bentuk kata kerja untuk waktu, jadi perbedaan ini sering membingungkan. The **past simple** talks about a finished action at a **finished time** (yesterday, in 2020, two years ago, last week). The **present perfect** (have/has + past participle) connects the past to **now**: life experiences with no specific time, changes and results that matter now, and situations that started in the past and continue until now.

### Kapan memakai yang mana?
| Situasi | Tense | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Waktu selesai disebut | Past simple | I *moved* here in 2019. |
| Pengalaman, waktu tidak penting | Present perfect | I *have lived* abroad. |
| Hasil yang terlihat sekarang | Present perfect | She *has cut* her hair. |
| Masih berlanjut sampai sekarang | Present perfect + for/since | We *have known* each other since 2015. |
| Baru saja / sudah / belum | Present perfect + just/already/yet | He *hasn't replied* yet. |

### Kata kunci
Past simple: *yesterday, ago, last..., in + year, when...?* Present perfect: *ever, never, so far, recently, just, already, yet, for, since*. Remember: **never use ago or a finished time with the present perfect**. A common pattern in conversation is to open with the present perfect and continue with the past simple for details: *Have you ever been to Port Selwyn? — Yes, I went there last summer.*

formulas.label: Present perfect (+)
formulas.pattern: Subject + have/has + past participle

formulas.label: Present perfect (−)
formulas.pattern: Subject + haven't/hasn't + past participle

formulas.label: Present perfect (?)
formulas.pattern: Have/Has + subject + past participle ...?

formulas.label: Past simple (+)
formulas.pattern: Subject + verb-ed / irregular past form

formulas.label: Duration
formulas.pattern: have/has + past participle + for (a period) / since (a starting point)

positive: Nadia has worked at the hospital since 2018.
I visited my grandparents last weekend.
We've just finished our final exams.
negative: Bayu hasn't found a new flat yet.
They didn't go to the wedding in March.
interrogative: Have you ever won a competition?
When did you graduate from university?

grammarTopics.comparison: Bandingkan: *I lost my phone yesterday* (fokus pada kejadian kemarin) vs *I've lost my phone* (fokus pada hasil sekarang: saya tidak punya ponsel). In questions with **When...?** always use the past simple.

mistakes.wrong: I have finished the report two hours ago.
mistakes.right: I finished the report two hours ago.
mistakes.why: *Ago* menunjukkan waktu yang sudah selesai, jadi pakai past simple.

mistakes.wrong: I live in this town since 2020.
mistakes.right: I have lived in this town since 2020.
mistakes.why: Situasi yang dimulai di masa lalu dan masih berlanjut memakai present perfect, bukan present simple.

mistakes.wrong: When have you started your new job?
mistakes.right: When did you start your new job?
mistakes.why: Pertanyaan *When* menanyakan waktu spesifik → past simple.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct option: Mira ___ in Port Selwyn since she was twelve.
exercises.explanation: *Since she was twelve* menunjukkan situasi yang dimulai di masa lalu dan masih berlanjut. With **since** we use the present perfect: *has lived*.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the correct form of the verbs in brackets.
exercises.text: We ___ (not / see) Pak Darto since the meeting last month, but he ___ (call) me yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Gap 1: *since the meeting* → present perfect negatif **haven't seen**. Gap 2: *yesterday* is a finished time → past simple **called**.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake in the sentence.
exercises.explanation: *Last weekend* adalah waktu yang sudah selesai, jadi harus past simple: **bought**. The present perfect cannot be used with a finished time expression.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it means the same.
exercises.sentence: I started playing the guitar three years ago (and I still play it).
exercises.cue: Use for. Begin with: I have ...
answers: I have played the guitar for three years.
I've played the guitar for three years.
I have been playing the guitar for three years.
I've been playing the guitar for three years.
exercises.explanation: *Started ... three years ago* + masih berlanjut → present perfect + **for three years** (durasi). Ago → for when we change past simple into present perfect.

grammarTopics.title: Narrative Tenses: Past Simple, Past Continuous and Past Perfect
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Tiga tense untuk bercerita
When we tell a story in English, we usually combine three past tenses. Masing-masing punya tugas yang berbeda:

| Tense | Fungsi | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Past continuous | Latar/background, aksi yang sedang berlangsung | The sun *was shining* and birds *were singing*. |
| Past simple | Kejadian utama, berurutan | I *opened* the door and *saw* a stranger. |
| Past perfect | Kejadian yang terjadi **lebih dulu** dari titik cerita | He *had left* before I arrived. |

### Past continuous + past simple
A longer action in progress is often interrupted by a short action: *I was cooking when the phone rang.* Gunakan **while** sebelum aksi panjang dan **when** sebelum aksi pendek.

### Past perfect (had + past participle)
The past perfect shows the **earlier** of two past events. Bandingkan:
- *When I arrived, the film started.* (saya datang → film mulai)
- *When I arrived, the film had started.* (film sudah mulai sebelum saya datang)

Common time words: *by the time, already, before, after, never ... before, just*. You do not need the past perfect when the order is already clear with *after* or *before*, but it is never wrong for the earlier action.

### Tips bercerita
Start with background (past continuous), move the story forward with the past simple, and jump back in time with the past perfect. Connectors such as *suddenly, luckily, unfortunately* and *in the end* make your story easier to follow.

formulas.label: Past continuous
formulas.pattern: Subject + was/were + verb-ing

formulas.label: Past perfect (+)
formulas.pattern: Subject + had + past participle

formulas.label: Past perfect (−)
formulas.pattern: Subject + hadn't + past participle

formulas.label: Interrupted action
formulas.pattern: While + past continuous, past simple / Past continuous + when + past simple

positive: It was raining heavily when we left the cinema.
By the time the police arrived, the thief had escaped.
Lina had never seen snow before her trip to the mountains.
negative: I hadn't finished my homework when my friends called.
We weren't watching TV when the lights went out.
interrogative: What were you doing when the earthquake started?
Had you ever met him before the party?

grammarTopics.comparison: *When I got to the station, the train left* (saya lihat kereta berangkat) vs *When I got to the station, the train had left* (kereta sudah pergi, saya terlambat).

mistakes.wrong: When I arrived, everyone had went home.
mistakes.right: When I arrived, everyone had gone home.
mistakes.why: Past perfect memakai past participle (*gone*), bukan bentuk past simple (*went*).

mistakes.wrong: While I walked home, I was seeing an accident.
mistakes.right: While I was walking home, I saw an accident.
mistakes.why: Aksi panjang (latar) memakai past continuous; aksi pendek yang menyela memakai past simple.

mistakes.wrong: She was knowing the answer.
mistakes.right: She knew the answer.
mistakes.why: Stative verbs seperti *know* tidak dipakai dalam bentuk continuous.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct verb forms.
exercises.text: When we ___ at the cinema, the film ___. We missed the first ten minutes.
exercises.explanation: Kedatangan kami adalah titik cerita (past simple **arrived**). The film started **before** that, so we use the past perfect **had already started**.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: It ___ (rain) heavily when Sinta left the office, so she opened her umbrella.
exercises.explanation: Hujan adalah latar yang sedang berlangsung saat Sinta keluar → past continuous **was raining**. The short action *left* is in the past simple.

exercises.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order to make a sentence.
fragments: By the time the firefighters arrived,
acceptedAnswers: The neighbours had already put out the fire by the time the firefighters arrived.
exercises.explanation: *By the time* + past simple, lalu past perfect untuk aksi yang selesai lebih dulu. The neighbours finished before the firefighters came.

exercises.prompt: Which sentences are grammatically correct? Choose all that apply.
options: I was cooking dinner when the lights went out.
She had never flown before, so she felt nervous on the plane.
When I arrived, everyone had went home.
I didn't recognise him because he had grew a beard.
exercises.explanation: Kalimat 3 dan 4 salah karena past perfect harus memakai past participle: *had gone*, *had grown*. Sentences 1 and 2 use the narrative tenses correctly.

grammarTopics.title: Future Forms: Will, Be Going To, Present Continuous, Might/May
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Banyak cara membicarakan masa depan
Bahasa Inggris tidak punya satu future tense saja. The form you choose depends on **how certain** you are and **when** you made the decision.

| Bentuk | Fungsi | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| will | Keputusan spontan, janji, tawaran, prediksi berdasarkan pendapat | I think robots *will* do most housework one day. |
| be going to | Rencana yang sudah diputuskan; prediksi dengan bukti sekarang | Look at those clouds — it*'s going to* rain. |
| present continuous | Janji temu/arrangement yang sudah diatur (waktu, tempat, orang lain) | I*'m meeting* the dentist at 4 tomorrow. |
| might / may | Kemungkinan (sekitar 50% atau kurang) | We *might* move to a bigger flat next year. |

### Future time clauses
After **when, as soon as, before, after, until** we use the **present simple**, not *will*, even though the meaning is future. Ini sering salah karena dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang *ketika saya akan sampai*.
- *I'll text you **when I arrive**.* (bukan *when I will arrive*)
- *As soon as the results **are** ready, we'll send them to you.*

### Might and may
*Might* and *may* are followed by the **base form** without *to*: *It might rain* (bukan *might to rain*). The negative is *might not / may not*. Untuk tingkat kepastian, gunakan *will definitely* (pasti), *will probably* (mungkin besar), *might* (mungkin), *probably won't* (kemungkinan tidak).

formulas.label: will
formulas.pattern: Subject + will ('ll) + base verb

formulas.label: be going to
formulas.pattern: Subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb

formulas.label: Arrangement
formulas.pattern: Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing + future time

formulas.label: Time clause
formulas.pattern: When/As soon as/Before/After + present simple, will + base verb

formulas.label: Possibility
formulas.pattern: Subject + might/may (not) + base verb

positive: I'm flying to Kotabaru on Friday morning.
We're going to buy a new laptop next month.
Electric cars will probably become cheaper in the future.
negative: I won't tell anyone your secret, I promise.
Rudi might not come to the party because he's tired.
interrogative: What are you doing this weekend?
Will you call me as soon as you get home?

grammarTopics.comparison: *I'm going to visit my aunt* (rencana pribadi) vs *I'm visiting my aunt on Sunday* (sudah diatur dengan bibi, waktunya jelas). Both are possible for plans; the present continuous emphasises a fixed arrangement.

mistakes.wrong: I'll call you when I will arrive at the hotel.
mistakes.right: I'll call you when I arrive at the hotel.
mistakes.why: Setelah *when* dalam future time clause, gunakan present simple.

mistakes.wrong: It might to snow tonight.
mistakes.right: It might snow tonight.
mistakes.why: *Might* langsung diikuti base verb tanpa *to*.

mistakes.wrong: A: The phone is ringing. B: I'm going to answer it!
mistakes.right: A: The phone is ringing. B: I'll answer it!
mistakes.why: Keputusan spontan pada saat berbicara memakai *will*.

exercises.prompt: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain.
exercises.explanation: Ada bukti sekarang (awan hitam) → **be going to** untuk prediksi. *Might to* dan *is raining to* tidak gramatikal.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best future form for each gap.
exercises.text: A: The phone's ringing! B: Don't worry, I ___ it. A: Thanks. Are you free on Saturday, by the way? B: Sorry, I'm not. I ___ my cousin's wedding in Kotabaru. We booked the train tickets last week.
exercises.explanation: Gap 1: keputusan spontan → **'ll get**. Gap 2: an arrangement that is already fixed (tickets are booked) → present continuous **'m attending**.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the correct form of the verbs in brackets.
exercises.text: As soon as the new app ___ (be) ready, we ___ (send) you a link.
exercises.explanation: Setelah *as soon as* pakai present simple (**is**), dan di klausa utama pakai **will send**. Never use *will* directly after *as soon as*.

exercises.prompt: Correct the mistake in the sentence.
exercises.sentence: I'm not sure yet, but we may to move to Port Selwyn next year.
answers: I'm not sure yet, but we may move to Port Selwyn next year.
I am not sure yet, but we may move to Port Selwyn next year.
exercises.explanation: *May* adalah modal verb, jadi langsung diikuti base verb: **may move**. Modal verbs never take *to* after them (except *ought to* and *have to*).

grammarTopics.title: Zero and First Conditional, Unless and As Long As
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Kondisi yang nyata
Real conditionals talk about situations that are true in general or **possible** in the future. Kalimat *if* terdiri dari dua bagian: the **if-clause** (syarat) and the **main clause** (hasil). The order can change; use a comma when the if-clause comes first.

| Jenis | Bentuk | Fungsi | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Zero conditional | If + present simple, present simple | Fakta umum, hukum alam, kebiasaan | If you heat ice, it melts. |
| First conditional | If + present simple, will + base verb | Kemungkinan nyata di masa depan | If it rains, we'll stay at home. |

### If vs when
*When* is used for things we are **sure** will happen; *if* is for things that **may or may not** happen. *When I get home, I'll cook* (pasti pulang) vs *If I get home early, I'll cook* (belum tentu).

### Unless and as long as
- **unless** = *if ... not*: *You won't pass unless you study.* = *If you don't study, you won't pass.* Jangan gunakan *not* lagi setelah *unless*.
- **as long as** = *only if* (syarat): *You can borrow my bike as long as you bring it back tonight.*

### Ingat!
Do not use *will* in the if-clause: *If it **rains** tomorrow* (bukan *If it will rain*). In the main clause you can also use other modals or the imperative: *If you feel tired, take a break. If we leave now, we might catch the bus.*

formulas.label: Zero conditional
formulas.pattern: If/When + present simple, present simple

formulas.label: First conditional
formulas.pattern: If + present simple, will/won't + base verb

formulas.label: Unless
formulas.pattern: Main clause + unless + present simple (positive meaning 'if not')

formulas.label: As long as
formulas.pattern: Main clause + as long as + present simple

positive: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
If we recycle more, there will be less rubbish in the sea.
You can stay out late as long as you call us.
negative: If you don't water plants, they die.
We won't finish on time unless everyone helps.
interrogative: What will you do if the bus doesn't come?
Will you help me if I get stuck?

grammarTopics.comparison: Zero conditional = selalu benar (*If you press this button, the machine stops*). First conditional = satu situasi spesifik di masa depan (*If you press that button now, the machine will stop*).

mistakes.wrong: If it will rain tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.
mistakes.right: If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.
mistakes.why: Klausa *if* memakai present simple walaupun maknanya masa depan.

mistakes.wrong: Unless you don't hurry, you'll be late.
mistakes.right: Unless you hurry, you'll be late.
mistakes.why: *Unless* sudah berarti *if not*, jadi tidak perlu *don't*.

mistakes.wrong: If you will heat water to 100°C, it boils.
mistakes.right: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils.
mistakes.why: Zero conditional memakai present simple di kedua klausa.

exercises.prompt: If you leave butter in the sun, it ___.
exercises.explanation: Fakta umum → zero conditional: present simple di kedua klausa (**melts**). This is always true, not a single future event.

exercises.prompt: Complete the first conditional sentence with the verbs in brackets.
exercises.text: If we ___ (not / leave) now, we ___ (miss) the last ferry.
exercises.explanation: Klausa *if* → present simple (**don't leave**); main clause → **will miss**. This is a real possibility in the future.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using unless.
exercises.sentence: If you don't book early, you won't get a seat.
exercises.cue: Begin with: You won't get a seat ...
answers: You won't get a seat unless you book early.
You will not get a seat unless you book early.
exercises.explanation: *If you don't book* = **unless you book**. Setelah *unless* kalimatnya positif.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct linking word.
exercises.text: You can borrow my camera ___ you bring it back by Friday.
exercises.explanation: **As long as** = dengan syarat (*only if*). *Unless* would mean 'if you don't bring it back', which makes no sense here.

grammarTopics.title: Second Conditional and I Wish
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Situasi tidak nyata atau imajiner
The **second conditional** describes situations that are **unreal, imaginary or very unlikely** now or in the future. Walaupun kata kerjanya berbentuk past, maknanya **bukan** masa lalu.

| Bagian | Bentuk | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| If-clause | If + past simple | If I *had* more money, |
| Main clause | would/could + base verb | I *would travel* around the world. |

### Were untuk semua subjek
In formal and written English we often use **were** for all subjects: *If I were rich...*, *If she were here...* The phrase **If I were you, I'd...** is a common way to give advice. (*If I was...* is common in informal speech.)

### First vs second conditional
- *If I **win** the race, I'll buy everyone a drink.* → mungkin terjadi (saya sedang ikut lomba).
- *If I **won** the lottery, I'd buy a house.* → kecil kemungkinannya / khayalan.

The choice depends on how **realistic** the speaker thinks the situation is.

### I wish + past simple
Use **I wish + past simple** for present situations that you would like to be different. Artinya: kenyataan sekarang **berlawanan**.
- *I wish I **had** a car.* (Kenyataannya: saya tidak punya mobil.)
- *I wish I **could** speak Japanese.* (Saya tidak bisa.)
- *I wish it **weren't** so hot today.* (Hari ini sangat panas.)

Jangan pakai *will* atau *would* setelah *If* dalam second conditional, and use *could* (not *can*) after *I wish*.

formulas.label: Second conditional
formulas.pattern: If + past simple, would/could + base verb

formulas.label: Advice
formulas.pattern: If I were you, I would ('d) + base verb

formulas.label: Present wish
formulas.pattern: I wish + subject + past simple / could + base verb

positive: If I lived by the sea, I would go swimming every morning.
If I were you, I'd talk to your manager.
I wish I knew the answer.
negative: If he didn't work so much, he wouldn't be so tired.
I wish my flat weren't so small.
interrogative: What would you do if you found a wallet in the street?
If you could live anywhere, where would you live?

grammarTopics.comparison: *If it's sunny tomorrow, we'll go to the beach* (nyata, mungkin) vs *If I had wings, I'd fly to the beach* (tidak mungkin).

mistakes.wrong: If I would have more time, I would learn to dive.
mistakes.right: If I had more time, I would learn to dive.
mistakes.why: Klausa *if* dalam second conditional memakai past simple, bukan *would*.

mistakes.wrong: I wish I can speak Japanese fluently.
mistakes.right: I wish I could speak Japanese fluently.
mistakes.why: Setelah *I wish*, *can* berubah menjadi *could*.

mistakes.wrong: If I am you, I would apologise.
mistakes.right: If I were you, I would apologise.
mistakes.why: Ungkapan saran yang tetap adalah *If I were you*.

exercises.prompt: If I ___ more free time, I would learn to play the piano.
exercises.explanation: Second conditional: **If + past simple** (*had*), lalu *would + base verb*. The situation is imaginary — I don't have much free time now.

exercises.prompt: Complete the advice with the verbs in brackets.
exercises.text: If I ___ (be) you, I ___ (apologise) to her before the party.
exercises.explanation: Ungkapan saran: **If I were you, I would/I'd...** *Was* is also heard in informal English, but *were* is the standard form.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake in the sentence.
exercises.explanation: Setelah *I wish* untuk situasi sekarang, gunakan bentuk past: *can* → **could**.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings with the correct endings.

pairs.left: If I lived by the sea,
pairs.right: I would go swimming every morning.

pairs.left: If you mix red and white,

exercises.explanation: Present simple + *will* = first conditional; past simple + *would* = second conditional; present + present = zero conditional (fakta); *I wish* + past simple = keinginan tentang sekarang.

grammarTopics.title: Modals: Obligation, Advice and Deduction
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Obligation (kewajiban)
| Modal | Makna | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| must | Kewajiban kuat, sering dari pembicara/aturan tertulis | You *must* wear a helmet. |
| have to | Kewajiban dari luar (aturan, hukum) | I *have to* start work at 7. |
| need to | Perlu | You *need to* renew your passport. |
| mustn't | **Dilarang** | You *mustn't* smoke here. |
| don't have to / don't need to | **Tidak perlu** (boleh, tapi tidak wajib) | You *don't have to* bring food. |

Perhatikan: *mustn't* dan *don't have to* sangat berbeda! *Mustn't* = it is not allowed. *Don't have to* = it is not necessary. For the past, use **had to**: *I had to work late yesterday* (there is no past form of *must* for obligation).

### Advice (saran)
**Should** and **ought to** give advice and have almost the same meaning: *You should / ought to see a doctor.* **Had better ('d better)** is stronger and suggests a problem if you don't follow the advice: *You'd better leave now or you'll miss the train.* Negative: *had better not* (bukan *hadn't better*).

### Deduction (menyimpulkan tentang sekarang)
- **must** = saya yakin benar (*He must be tired — he worked all night.*)
- **might / may / could** = mungkin (*She might be at the library.*)
- **can't** = saya yakin tidak benar (*That can't be Tono — he's in Kotabaru.*)

For deduction, the opposite of *must* is **can't**, not *mustn't*.

formulas.label: Obligation
formulas.pattern: must / have to / need to + base verb

formulas.label: No obligation
formulas.pattern: don't/doesn't have to / don't need to + base verb

formulas.label: Prohibition
formulas.pattern: mustn't + base verb

formulas.label: Advice
formulas.pattern: should / ought to / had better (not) + base verb

formulas.label: Deduction
formulas.pattern: must / might / can't + be / base verb

positive: All visitors must sign in at reception.
You ought to back up your files every week.
She must be very proud of her son.
negative: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.
We don't have to wear a uniform on Fridays.
That can't be the right address — it's a car park.
interrogative: Do we have to bring our own laptops?
Should I tell my manager about the mistake?

grammarTopics.comparison: *You mustn't park here* (dilarang) vs *You don't have to park here* (tidak wajib, ada pilihan lain). In deduction: *must be* (pasti ya) vs *can't be* (pasti tidak).

mistakes.wrong: You don't have to touch the machines — it's dangerous.
mistakes.right: You mustn't touch the machines — it's dangerous.
mistakes.why: Untuk larangan gunakan *mustn't*; *don't have to* berarti tidak perlu.

mistakes.wrong: He mustn't be at home — his car isn't there.
mistakes.right: He can't be at home — his car isn't there.
mistakes.why: Kesimpulan negatif (pasti tidak) memakai *can't*, bukan *mustn't*.

mistakes.wrong: You had better to see a doctor.
mistakes.right: You had better see a doctor.
mistakes.why: *Had better* langsung diikuti base verb tanpa *to*.

exercises.prompt: Which sentences mean 'It is not necessary to wear a tie'? Choose all that apply.
options: You don't have to wear a tie.
You don't need to wear a tie.
exercises.explanation: **Don't have to** dan **don't need to** = tidak perlu. *Mustn't* = dilarang, and *shouldn't* = it's a bad idea.

exercises.prompt: Raka has been at work since 6 a.m. and hasn't eaten anything. He ___ be hungry.
exercises.explanation: Ada bukti kuat → kesimpulan yakin: **must be**. *Can't* would mean we are sure he is not hungry, which is illogical here.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the negative form of had better.
exercises.text: The roads are very icy tonight. You ___ drive home — stay with us instead.
exercises.explanation: Bentuk negatif *had better* adalah **had better not** ('d better not), bukan *hadn't better*. It gives strong advice about a dangerous situation.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best reply.

dialogue.speaker: Ari
dialogue.text: Whose phone is this? It's got a cat sticker on the back.

options: It must be Nadia's. She loves cats.
It can't be Nadia's. She loves cats.
It must Nadia's. She loves cats.
It might to be Nadia's. She loves cats.
exercises.explanation: Bukti (Nadia suka kucing) → **must be** Nadia's. *Can't be* contradicts the evidence, and *must Nadia's* / *might to be* are ungrammatical.

grammarTopics.title: The Passive: Present Simple and Past Simple
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Apa itu passive?
In an active sentence, the subject **does** the action: *Workers **pack** the tea.* In a passive sentence, the subject **receives** the action: *The tea **is packed** by workers.* Mirip dengan bentuk *di-* dalam bahasa Indonesia (*teh dikemas oleh pekerja*).

### Bentuk
| Tense | Active | Passive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Present simple | They *make* paper from wood. | Paper *is made* from wood. |
| Past simple | Someone *stole* my bike. | My bike *was stolen*. |

Passive = **be** (sesuai tense dan subjek) + **past participle**. Negatives and questions are made with *be*: *It **isn't** made in this country. **Was** the bridge built in 1990? **When was** it built?*

### Kapan memakai passive?
- When the action or result is more important than the person who does it (proses, produk, sejarah).
- When we don't know who did it, or it is obvious: *My wallet was stolen. Rice is grown in many parts of Asia.*
- In descriptions of processes: *First, the beans are cleaned. Then they are roasted.*

### By + agent
Use **by** only when the agent (pelaku) is important or new information: *The museum was designed **by** a famous local architect.* Jangan tambahkan *by people / by someone / by them* — informasi itu tidak berguna.

Catatan: hanya kata kerja yang punya objek (transitive verbs) yang bisa dibuat passive. *Happen, arrive, die* tidak bisa dipasifkan.

formulas.label: Present simple passive
formulas.pattern: am/is/are + past participle

formulas.label: Past simple passive
formulas.pattern: was/were + past participle

formulas.label: Negative
formulas.pattern: isn't/aren't/wasn't/weren't + past participle

formulas.label: Question
formulas.pattern: (Wh-) + am/is/are/was/were + subject + past participle?

formulas.label: Agent
formulas.pattern: ... + by + agent

positive: Most of our vegetables are grown on local farms.
The old station was turned into a museum in 2015.
This song was written by my uncle.
negative: The letters weren't delivered on time.
Plastic bags aren't used in this supermarket anymore.
interrogative: Where are these phones made?
Was anyone hurt in the accident?

grammarTopics.comparison: Active: *A young engineer designed the bridge.* (fokus pada insinyur) — Passive: *The bridge was designed by a young engineer.* (fokus pada jembatan)

mistakes.wrong: The bridge was build in 1998.
mistakes.right: The bridge was built in 1998.
mistakes.why: Passive memakai past participle (*built*), bukan base verb.

mistakes.wrong: The accident was happened at night.
mistakes.right: The accident happened at night.
mistakes.why: *Happen* tidak punya objek, jadi tidak bisa dipasifkan.

mistakes.wrong: The letter was wrote by my sister.
mistakes.right: The letter was written by my sister.
mistakes.why: Passive selalu memakai be + past participle (V3). The past participle of write is written, not wrote.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the present simple passive of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: In our factory, the bottles ___ (wash) and then they ___ (fill) with juice.
exercises.explanation: Proses → present simple passive: **are + past participle** (*are washed, are filled*). The subject *bottles* is plural, so we use *are*.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the passive.
exercises.sentence: A young engineer designed the bridge in 1998.
answers: The bridge was designed by a young engineer in 1998.
The bridge was designed in 1998 by a young engineer.
exercises.explanation: Past simple active → **was + past participle**. The agent is new information, so we keep **by a young engineer**.

exercises.prompt: When ___ this temple built?
exercises.explanation: Pertanyaan passive memakai *be*, bukan *did*. *Temple* is singular and the building happened in the past → **was**.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake in the sentence.
exercises.explanation: Passive membutuhkan past participle: **are produced**, bukan base verb *produce*.

grammarTopics.title: Defining Relative Clauses
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Fungsi relative clause
A defining relative clause tells us **exactly which** person, thing or place we mean. Tanpa klausa ini, kalimatnya tidak jelas: *The woman is a pilot* (wanita yang mana?) → *The woman **who lives next door** is a pilot.*

### Relative pronouns
| Pronoun | Untuk | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| who / that | orang | The man *who* fixed my car was very friendly. |
| which / that | benda, hewan | The bag *which* I bought is too small. |
| where | tempat | That's the café *where* we first met. |
| whose | kepemilikan (punya siapa) | I have a friend *whose* father is a chef. |
| when | waktu | I remember the day *when* we moved here. |

### Menghilangkan pronoun
You can leave out *who/which/that* when it is the **object** of the relative clause — that is, when another subject follows it:
- *The book (that) **I** borrowed was great.* → boleh dihilangkan.
- *The man **who called** you is my uncle.* → tidak boleh, karena *who* adalah subjek dari *called*.

### Hal penting
- Do not repeat the pronoun: *The phone which I bought ~~it~~ is broken.* Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita kadang mengulang (*yang saya beli itu*), tetapi dalam bahasa Inggris tidak.
- *Whose* is followed by a noun: *the girl whose bike was stolen*.
- Defining relative clauses do not use commas.

formulas.label: People
formulas.pattern: noun + who/that + verb ...

formulas.label: Things
formulas.pattern: noun + which/that + verb ...

formulas.label: Place / possession / time
formulas.pattern: noun + where/whose + noun/when + clause

formulas.label: Object pronoun omitted
formulas.pattern: noun + (that/which/who) + subject + verb

positive: A chef is a person who cooks in a restaurant.
This is the village where my grandmother was born.
The jacket I bought last week is already torn.
negative: I don't like films that have sad endings.
He isn't the teacher whose class I joined.
interrogative: Is this the hotel where you stayed last year?
Do you know anyone who speaks Korean?

grammarTopics.comparison: *The film **that** we watched* (that = object, boleh dihilangkan: *the film we watched*) vs *the film **that** won the prize* (that = subject, tidak boleh dihilangkan).

mistakes.wrong: The man which helped me was very kind.
mistakes.right: The man who helped me was very kind.
mistakes.why: Untuk orang gunakan *who* atau *that*, bukan *which*.

mistakes.wrong: This is the shop which I bought my phone.
mistakes.right: This is the shop where I bought my phone.
mistakes.why: Untuk tempat (di mana sesuatu terjadi) gunakan *where*.

mistakes.wrong: The cake that I made it was delicious.
mistakes.right: The cake that I made was delicious.
mistakes.why: Jangan mengulang objek (*it*) di dalam relative clause.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct relative words.
exercises.text: The woman ___ lives next door is a pilot. The café ___ we first met has closed down.
exercises.explanation: Orang → **who**. Tempat di mana sesuatu terjadi → **where**. *The café which we first met* is wrong because *met* needs a place adverbial, not an object.

exercises.prompt: In which sentences can you leave out the relative pronoun? Choose all that apply.
options: The book that I borrowed from Tono was great.
The man who called you is my uncle.
The film which we watched last night was scary.
The dog that bit the postman belongs to Mr. Ruslan.
exercises.explanation: Pronoun boleh dihilangkan jika ia objek (diikuti subjek lain: *I borrowed*, *we watched*). In sentences 2 and 4, *who/that* is the subject of *called/bit*, so it must stay.

exercises.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order.
exercises.explanation: *Where* memperkenalkan klausa tentang tempat: *the hotel where my parents stayed*. The relative clause comes directly after the noun it describes.

exercises.prompt: Complete the definition with one relative pronoun.
exercises.text: A thermometer is a device ___ measures temperature.
exercises.explanation: Benda → **which** atau **that**. The pronoun is the subject of *measures*, so it cannot be left out.

grammarTopics.title: Reported Speech: Statements, Questions, Say and Tell
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Melaporkan perkataan orang lain
When we report what someone said, the tense usually moves **one step back** (backshift), because the words were said in the past. Pronoun dan keterangan waktu juga berubah sesuai situasi.

| Direct speech | Reported speech |
| --- | --- |
| present simple: *I am tired.* | past simple: She said she *was* tired. |
| present continuous: *I'm working.* | past continuous: He said he *was working*. |
| past simple / present perfect: *I've finished / I finished.* | past perfect: She said she *had finished*. |
| will: *I'll help.* | would: He said he *would help*. |
| can: *I can swim.* | could: She said she *could swim*. |

Time words: *today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there, this → that*.

### Reported questions
In reported questions we use **statement word order** (subjek + kata kerja) and **no do/does/did**, no question mark.
- *Where do you work?* → He asked me where I **worked**.
- Yes/no questions use **if** or **whether**: *Are you ready?* → She asked if I **was** ready.

### Say vs tell
- **say** + (that) + clause: *She said (that) she was busy.* — *say to someone* juga bisa, tapi jarang.
- **tell** + **person** + (that) + clause: *She told **me** (that) she was busy.* *Tell* selalu membutuhkan objek orang.

Other useful reporting verbs: *explain, mention, reply, add, complain*.

formulas.label: Statement
formulas.pattern: Subject + said (that) / told + person + (that) + backshifted clause

formulas.label: Wh- question
formulas.pattern: Subject + asked (+ person) + wh-word + subject + verb

formulas.label: Yes/no question
formulas.pattern: Subject + asked (+ person) + if/whether + subject + verb

positive: Laila said she was tired.
Dimas told me that he had lost his wallet.
The receptionist asked us what time we wanted to check out.
negative: He said he didn't like spicy food.
She told us she wouldn't be at the meeting.
interrogative: What did the doctor say?
Did she tell you why she was late?

grammarTopics.comparison: *She said me...* ✗ → *She **told** me...* ✓ / *She **said** that...* ✓. Reported question: *He asked where I lived* ✓ (bukan *where did I live*).

mistakes.wrong: She said me that she was busy.
mistakes.right: She told me that she was busy.
mistakes.why: *Say* tidak langsung diikuti orang; gunakan *tell + person*.

mistakes.wrong: He asked me where did I live.
mistakes.right: He asked me where I lived.
mistakes.why: Reported question memakai susunan kalimat pernyataan, tanpa *did*.

mistakes.wrong: She asked me do I like coffee.
mistakes.right: She asked me if I liked coffee.
mistakes.why: Yes/no question dilaporkan dengan *if/whether* + susunan pernyataan.

exercises.prompt: Report the sentence. Use tense backshift.
exercises.sentence: "I can't find my glasses," said Grandma.
answers: Grandma said she couldn't find her glasses.
Grandma said that she couldn't find her glasses.
Grandma said she could not find her glasses.
Grandma said that she could not find her glasses.
exercises.explanation: *Can't* → **couldn't**, dan *my* → **her**. The word *that* is optional after *said*.

exercises.prompt: Dimas ___ me that he had lost his wallet.
exercises.explanation: Setelah kosong ada orang (*me*) lalu klausa → **told**. *Said*, *spoke* and *talked* cannot be followed directly by a person + that-clause.

exercises.prompt: Report the question. Use tense backshift.
exercises.context: "Do you work on Saturdays?" the manager asked me.
exercises.text: The manager asked me ___ I ___ on Saturdays.
exercises.explanation: Yes/no question → **if/whether**; *do you work* → **I worked** (susunan pernyataan, tanpa *do*).

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake in the sentence.
exercises.explanation: Dalam reported question tidak ada *did* dan susunannya subjek + kata kerja: **where I had bought** (or *where I bought*).

grammarTopics.title: Verb Patterns, Used To and Be/Get Used To
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Verb + -ing atau verb + to-infinitive?
Some verbs are followed by **-ing**, others by **to + base verb**. Tidak ada aturan pasti, jadi pelajari sebagai pasangan (chunks).

| + -ing | + to-infinitive |
| --- | --- |
| enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, keep, suggest, give up, consider | want, decide, hope, plan, agree, refuse, afford, manage, promise |

Some verbs, such as *like, love, hate, start, begin*, can take both with little change in meaning. Setelah **preposisi** (about, of, at, before, after, without) selalu gunakan **-ing**: *I'm thinking **about moving***.

### Used to + base verb (kebiasaan masa lalu)
**Used to** describes past habits or states that are **no longer true**. Dalam bahasa Indonesia mirip dengan *dulu (sering)...*
- *I **used to** play football every afternoon.* (sekarang tidak lagi)
- Negative: *I **didn't use to** like vegetables.* Question: ***Did** you **use to** live here?* (tanpa *-d* setelah *did*)

### Be used to / get used to + -ing / noun
These have a **different meaning**: *be used to* = sudah terbiasa; *get used to* = mulai terbiasa (proses).
- *I'**m used to getting** up early.* (sudah biasa)
- *It took me months to **get used to** the cold weather.* (proses menjadi biasa)

Note: in *be/get used to*, **to** is a preposition, so it is followed by **-ing** or a noun, not a base verb.

| Bentuk | Makna | Diikuti |
| --- | --- | --- |
| used to | dulu (sekarang tidak) | base verb |
| be used to | sudah terbiasa | -ing / noun |
| get used to | menjadi terbiasa | -ing / noun |

formulas.label: Verb + -ing
formulas.pattern: enjoy / avoid / finish / mind / give up + verb-ing

formulas.label: Verb + to-infinitive
formulas.pattern: want / decide / hope / plan / refuse + to + base verb

formulas.label: Past habit
formulas.pattern: used to / didn't use to + base verb

formulas.label: Familiarity
formulas.pattern: be / get used to + verb-ing / noun

positive: I've decided to take up yoga.
My grandfather used to walk five kilometres to school.
Ana is used to working at night now.
negative: We didn't use to have a car.
I can't get used to driving on the left.
interrogative: Did you use to have long hair?
Would you mind closing the window?

grammarTopics.comparison: *I used to live alone* (dulu, sekarang tidak) vs *I'm used to living alone* (sudah terbiasa sekarang).

mistakes.wrong: I enjoy to cook for my friends.
mistakes.right: I enjoy cooking for my friends.
mistakes.why: *Enjoy* selalu diikuti -ing.

mistakes.wrong: Did you used to play an instrument?
mistakes.right: Did you use to play an instrument?
mistakes.why: Setelah *did*, gunakan *use to* tanpa -d.

mistakes.wrong: I'm used to get up at 5 a.m.
mistakes.right: I'm used to getting up at 5 a.m.
mistakes.why: *To* dalam *be used to* adalah preposisi, jadi diikuti -ing.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct verb forms.
exercises.text: Rudi has decided ___ a new job, and he avoids ___ fast food because he wants to be healthier.
exercises.explanation: *Decide* + **to-infinitive** (*to look for*); *avoid* + **-ing** (*eating*).

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form of used to.
exercises.text: My grandfather ___ smoke, but he gave up ten years ago.
exercises.explanation: Kebiasaan masa lalu yang sudah berhenti → **used to + base verb**.

exercises.prompt: Ana moved to a cold country last year. At first it was hard, but now she ___ the cold weather.
exercises.explanation: Sekarang sudah terbiasa → **is used to** + noun. *Used to* alone would describe a past habit that is no longer true.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English. Use used to.
exercises.source: Dulu saya tidak suka sayur, tetapi sekarang saya menyukainya.
answers: I didn't use to like vegetables, but now I like them.
I didn't use to like vegetables, but now I do.
I didn't use to like vegetables, but I like them now.
I did not use to like vegetables, but now I like them.
I did not use to like vegetables, but now I do.
I did not use to like vegetables, but I like them now.
I never used to like vegetables, but now I like them.
I never used to like vegetables, but now I do.
I never used to like vegetables, but I like them now.
exercises.explanation: *Dulu tidak...* → **didn't use to** + base verb (tanpa -d setelah *didn't*). *Never used to* is also correct.

reading.title: Fix It, Don't Throw It Away
reading.body:
Every first Saturday of the month, the community hall in Millbrook becomes a very busy place. People arrive carrying broken lamps, torn jackets, old radios and bicycles with flat tyres. They have come to the Millbrook Repair Café, where volunteers fix things for free.

The café was started three years ago by Helen Marsh, a retired engineer. "I was tired of seeing perfectly good things in the rubbish bin," she explains. "Most of them only needed a small repair." Today, more than twenty volunteers help her. Some are electricians, some are good at sewing, and one is a former bicycle mechanic.

Visitors don't have to pay, but they are asked to stay and watch while their item is repaired. "We want people to learn," says Helen. "If you see how something is fixed, you might be able to do it yourself next time." Coffee and cake are sold at a small table, and the money is used to buy tools.

The café has become popular with young people, too. Twenty-year-old student Tom Reyes brought his laptop last month. "The shop told me I needed a new one," he says. "Here, they found a loose cable in ten minutes. I couldn't believe it."

According to the volunteers' records, around 1,500 items have been repaired since the café opened. That is a lot of waste that didn't end up in landfill. Helen hopes other towns will follow Millbrook's example. "You don't need a big budget," she says. "You just need people who are happy to share their skills."

questions.prompt: What is the article mainly about?
options: a place where volunteers repair people's things for free
a shop that sells second-hand electronics
a course that trains people to become engineers
a café that is famous for its coffee and cake
questions.explanation: Main idea: seluruh artikel membahas **Millbrook Repair Café**, tempat relawan memperbaiki barang secara gratis. Coffee and cake are only a small detail.

questions.prompt: Why are visitors asked to stay while their item is repaired?
options: so that they can learn how to fix things themselves
because they have to pay before they leave
because the volunteers need their help
so that they can buy coffee and cake
questions.explanation: Paragraf 3: *"We want people to learn ... you might be able to do it yourself next time."* Tujuannya agar pengunjung belajar.

questions.prompt: What can we infer about Tom's laptop?
options: It did not really need to be replaced.
It was too old to repair.
He bought it at the Repair Café.
The shop repaired it for free.
questions.explanation: Toko bilang dia butuh laptop baru, tetapi relawan hanya menemukan kabel yang longgar dalam sepuluh menit. So the laptop didn't need to be replaced — kita menyimpulkannya, tidak tertulis langsung.

questions.prompt: In the last paragraph, 'landfill' most likely means:
options: a place where rubbish is buried
a factory where new products are made
a shop that sells used items
a field where farmers grow food
questions.explanation: Konteksnya adalah *waste* (sampah) yang tidak berakhir di *landfill*. Jadi landfill adalah tempat sampah dikubur — **tempat pembuangan akhir**.

questions.prompt: What is the money from the coffee and cake used for?
questions.explanation: Paragraf 3: *the money is used to buy tools* — uangnya dipakai untuk membeli peralatan.

reading.title: The Wrong Stop
reading.body:
Maya had never felt so nervous. It was the morning of her first job interview, and she was sitting on the 7.15 train to Port Selwyn. She had prepared for days: she had read everything about the company, and she had practised her answers in front of the mirror the night before. But she hadn't slept well, and as the train was moving gently through the green countryside, her eyes slowly closed.

When she woke up, the train was standing at a small station that she didn't recognise. A sign on the platform said 'Ashby Junction'. Maya's heart sank. She had missed her stop, and the interview was starting in forty minutes.

She ran to the ticket office, but it was closed. While she was looking desperately at the timetable, an elderly man with a walking stick came up to her. "You look worried," he said kindly. Maya explained everything. The man smiled. "My daughter is driving to Port Selwyn in five minutes. I'm sure she can take you."

The daughter, a cheerful woman called Ruth, drove fast but carefully, and Maya arrived at the office with two minutes to spare. She was out of breath, but she was there. The receptionist took her into a meeting room — and Maya couldn't believe her eyes. Sitting behind the desk was Ruth.

"Well," Ruth laughed, "at least I already know that you can stay calm when things go wrong." The interview went brilliantly, and a week later Maya got the job. She never fell asleep on a train again.

glossary.meaning: hatiku langsung lemas / kecewa dan cemas

questions.prompt: What is the best summary of the story?
options: A woman misses her stop on the way to an interview, but a stranger's help leads to a happy ending.
A woman decides not to go to her interview because she is too nervous.
An old man gets lost at a small station, and a young woman helps him.
A woman fails an interview because she arrives late.
questions.explanation: Maya tertidur dan terlewat stasiunnya, lalu seorang bapak tua dan putrinya membantu. In the end she gets the job — akhir yang bahagia.

questions.prompt: Why did Maya fall asleep on the train?
options: She hadn't slept well the night before.
She had worked late the night before.
The journey was very long and boring.
questions.explanation: Paragraf 1: *But she hadn't slept well* — perhatikan past perfect untuk menjelaskan sebab yang terjadi lebih dulu.

questions.prompt: Why did Ruth say she already knew that Maya could stay calm when things went wrong?
options: She had seen how Maya solved a stressful problem that morning.
She had read about Maya in the company's records.
Maya had told her about her past jobs in the car.
She had interviewed Maya once before.
questions.explanation: Ruth adalah orang yang mengantar Maya. She saw Maya deal with missing her stop and still arrive on time, jadi Ruth sudah melihat sendiri bagaimana Maya menghadapi masalah.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 2, 'Maya's heart sank' means that she suddenly felt:
questions.explanation: Kalimat berikutnya menjelaskan dia terlewat stasiun dan wawancaranya 40 menit lagi. *My heart sank* = tiba-tiba merasa cemas dan kecewa.

questions.prompt: When did Maya arrive at the office?
options: five minutes after the interview started
questions.explanation: *Maya arrived at the office with two minutes to spare* = dia tiba dua menit sebelum wawancara dimulai.

reading.title: Greetings from Northfield
reading.body:
Subject: Greetings from Northfield!

Hi Anisa,

Sorry I haven't written for so long! It's been a crazy month. As you know, I started my new job at the Northfield Science Museum three weeks ago, and I'm finally starting to feel at home.

The job is great, but there are a lot of rules. We have to wear a uniform – a dark green shirt with the museum logo – and we must wear our ID badges at all times. We aren't allowed to use our phones when we're with visitors, and that was hard at first, because I used to check my phone every five minutes! The good news is that we don't have to work on Mondays, because the museum is closed.

The weather is the biggest challenge. It's so cold here! I'm not used to wearing three layers of clothes, and it gets dark at four o'clock in the afternoon. My colleagues say I'll get used to it, but I'm not so sure. On the other hand, the people are really friendly. Last weekend my manager invited me to her house for dinner, and her husband cooked an amazing fish soup.

How are things with you? Have you finished your course yet? You should come and visit in the spring – it must be beautiful here when the snow melts. You could stay in my flat. The sofa is quite comfortable!

Write soon,
Dewi

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Dewi's email?
options: to tell her friend about her new job and life
to complain to her manager about the rules
to apply for a job at a museum
to ask her friend for advice about cold weather
questions.explanation: Dewi menulis kepada temannya tentang pekerjaan baru, aturan, cuaca dan rekan kerja. It's a friendly news email, bukan keluhan atau lamaran kerja.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a rule at Dewi's workplace?
options: Staff must wear an ID badge.
Staff have to wear a uniform.
Staff can't use their phones when they are with visitors.
questions.explanation: Dewi menulis *we don't have to work on Mondays, because the museum is closed*. Aturan lainnya disebutkan dalam paragraf 2.

questions.prompt: What can we infer about the place where Dewi lived before?
options: It had a science museum where she worked.
It got dark earlier than Northfield.
questions.explanation: Dewi *isn't used to* memakai tiga lapis pakaian dan mengeluh tentang dingin. So we can infer that her previous home was warmer.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 1, 'starting to feel at home' means Dewi is starting to:
options: feel comfortable and relaxed in the new place
want to go back to her own country
spend more time in her flat
feel tired after work every day
questions.explanation: *Feel at home* = merasa nyaman dan betah di suatu tempat, walaupun itu bukan rumahnya sendiri.

reading.title: Students' Solar Charger Wins National Prize
reading.body:
A group of four students from Greenhill Secondary School in Lakemoor has won first prize in this year's National Young Inventors Competition. Their invention, a low-cost solar charger for mobile phones, was chosen from more than 300 entries.

The charger is made from recycled materials, including old plastic bottles and parts from broken radios. It can charge a phone in about three hours on a sunny day. According to the team, each charger costs less than five dollars to produce.

The idea came from sixteen-year-old team member Farah Idris. She told reporters that her village often had power cuts and that her grandparents had once been unable to call a doctor because their phone battery was empty. "I wanted to find a simple solution that anyone could build," she said.

The students worked on the project for eight months, mostly after school and at weekends. Their science teacher, Mr. Colin Hart, said he had never seen such a determined group. "They failed many times," he explained, "but they never gave up."

The prize includes 10,000 dollars and a visit to a technology company. The team said they would use the money to build fifty chargers for families in their area. A local company has also asked whether it could produce the charger on a larger scale.

The competition is organised every year by the Young Science Council and is open to students aged 13 to 18.

questions.prompt: What is the news story mainly about?
options: students who won a prize for a cheap solar phone charger
a company that sells solar panels to schools
a village that often has power cuts
a science teacher who invented a new phone
questions.explanation: Judul dan paragraf pertama menyampaikan main idea: **empat siswa memenangkan lomba** dengan charger tenaga surya yang murah.

questions.prompt: What is the charger made from?
options: recycled materials such as plastic bottles and old radio parts
new parts bought from a technology company
glass and metal from old mobile phones
materials that cost more than five dollars each
questions.explanation: Paragraf 2: *The charger is made from recycled materials, including old plastic bottles and parts from broken radios* (present simple passive).

questions.prompt: Why was the project personally important to Farah?
options: Her own family had had problems because of power cuts.
She wanted to start her own technology company.
Her teacher asked her to find an idea for the competition.
Her grandparents worked in a radio factory.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 4, 'determined' is closest in meaning to:
options: not willing to stop trying, even when something is difficult
very intelligent and good at science
questions.explanation: Kalimat berikutnya menjelaskannya: *They failed many times, but they never gave up.* **Determined** = gigih, pantang menyerah.

questions.prompt: What did the team say they would do with the prize money?

buy new computers for their school

script.speaker: Rina
script.text: Hi, Tomi! Are you doing anything this weekend?

script.speaker: Tomi
script.text: Yes, I'm visiting my cousin in Port Selwyn on Saturday. My train leaves at nine.

script.speaker: Rina
script.text: Oh, nice. What are you going to do there?

script.speaker: Tomi
script.text: We're going to walk along the coast path if the weather's good. The forecast says it might rain in the afternoon, though.

script.speaker: Rina
script.text: Then you'd better take a raincoat! What about Sunday?

script.speaker: Tomi
script.text: I haven't decided yet. I might stay at home and study. I've got an exam on Tuesday.

script.speaker: Rina
script.text: Well, a few of us are going to the new Thai restaurant on Sunday evening. Do you want to come?

script.speaker: Tomi
script.text: That sounds great. If I finish my revision in time, I'll definitely join you. What time are you meeting?

script.speaker: Rina
script.text: At seven, outside the cinema. I'll send you the address as soon as I get home.

script.speaker: Tomi
script.text: Perfect. Thanks, Rina. See you on Sunday, I hope!

questions.prompt: What is Tomi doing on Saturday?
options: visiting his cousin in Port Selwyn
studying for his exam at home
questions.explanation: Tomi berkata *I'm visiting my cousin in Port Selwyn on Saturday* — present continuous untuk rencana yang sudah diatur (arrangement).

questions.prompt: Why might Tomi NOT go to the restaurant on Sunday?
options: He may need more time to study for his exam.
He will still be in Port Selwyn.
He doesn't know where the cinema is.
questions.explanation: *If I finish my revision in time, I'll definitely join you* — dia hanya ikut kalau belajarnya selesai. So he might need the time to study.

questions.prompt: What does Rina advise Tomi to take on Saturday?
questions.explanation: Rina berkata *you'd better take a raincoat* karena ramalan cuaca mengatakan mungkin hujan.

questions.prompt: Where and when are Rina and her friends meeting on Sunday?
options: at nine, at the train station
in the afternoon, on the coast path

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Good morning, Eastline Railways lost property office. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Adi
script.text: Hello. I left my bag on a train yesterday evening, and I was wondering if anyone had found it.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Which train were you on?

script.speaker: Adi
script.text: The 6.40 from Kotabaru to Lakemoor. I was reading a book when I suddenly realised it was my stop, so I jumped off quickly. I'd put the bag on the shelf above my seat, and I completely forgot about it.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Can you describe the bag, please?

script.speaker: Adi
script.text: It's a small black backpack with a red zip. There's a laptop inside, and a blue water bottle.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Just a moment, please. Yes, a black backpack was handed in by one of our cleaners last night. Does yours have a name tag?

script.speaker: Adi
script.text: Yes! It says 'A. Santoso'.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Then it must be yours. You can collect it from our office at Lakemoor Station. You'll need to bring some ID.

script.speaker: Adi
script.text: That's fantastic. When are you open?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: From eight in the morning until six in the evening, Monday to Saturday.

script.speaker: Adi
script.text: Great, I'll come this afternoon. Thank you so much!

questions.prompt: Why did Adi leave his bag on the train?
options: He got off in a hurry and forgot about it.
Someone took it while he was sleeping.
He gave it to a cleaner by mistake.
He left it at the ticket office.
questions.explanation: Adi sedang membaca, tiba-tiba sadar itu stasiunnya, lalu *jumped off quickly* dan lupa tasnya.

questions.prompt: Who found the bag?
questions.explanation: *A black backpack was handed in by one of our cleaners* — passive dengan by + agent.

questions.prompt: What does Adi need to bring when he collects the bag?
questions.explanation: Petugas berkata *You'll need to bring some ID* — ID = identification (kartu identitas).

questions.prompt: Why is the officer sure that the bag belongs to Adi?
options: It has a name tag with his name on it.
Adi knows the cleaner who found it.
Adi can describe the book inside it.
It was found on the 6.40 train from Lakemoor.
questions.explanation: Setelah Adi menyebut name tag *A. Santoso*, petugas membuat deduction: *Then it must be yours.*

script.text: Good morning, and welcome to Riverside Sports Centre. Please listen carefully to the following information.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Please note that the main swimming pool is closed for cleaning until two o'clock today. The small pool is open as usual.

script.speaker: Announcer

script.speaker: Announcer

questions.prompt: When will the main swimming pool open today?

questions.prompt: What is true about the yoga classes?
options: You don't have to book them before you come.

They are only for children under twelve.

questions.prompt: Where are visitors allowed to eat?
options: in the café on the first floor

questions.prompt: A ten-year-old girl wants to exercise at the centre. What can she do?
options: join a junior fitness class on Saturday morning
use the gym with her parents
use the gym after ten p.m.
nothing, because children aren't allowed in the centre

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Today I'm talking to Marco Lestari. He used to be an accountant in the city, and now he runs a small organic farm. Marco, what made you change?

script.speaker: Marco
script.text: Well, I used to spend ten hours a day in front of a computer, and I was always stressed. One day my doctor told me that I needed to change my lifestyle. That was when I decided to do something completely different.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Was it difficult at first?

script.speaker: Marco
script.text: Very! I wasn't used to physical work, so my back hurt every evening. And I had to learn everything about plants. I didn't even know how to grow tomatoes!

script.speaker: Host
script.text: And now?

script.speaker: Marco
script.text: Now I'm used to getting up at five, and I really enjoy working outside. I've lost ten kilos, and I sleep much better.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Do you miss anything about your old life?

script.speaker: Marco
script.text: I miss seeing my old colleagues, but I definitely don't miss the traffic. I used to spend two hours commuting every day.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: What advice would you give to listeners who are thinking about a big change?

script.speaker: Marco
script.text: Don't expect it to be easy. But if you really want it, you should try. You can always go back.

questions.prompt: What was Marco's job before he became a farmer?
questions.explanation: *He used to be an accountant in the city* — used to untuk keadaan di masa lalu.

questions.prompt: Why did Marco decide to change his life?
options: His doctor told him he needed a different lifestyle.
He lost his job at the office.
He wanted to earn more money.
questions.explanation: Reported speech: *my doctor told me that I needed to change my lifestyle.*

questions.prompt: What was difficult for Marco at the beginning?
options: He wasn't used to physical work.
He had to get up at five.
questions.explanation: *I wasn't used to physical work, so my back hurt every evening* — be used to untuk sesuatu yang sudah biasa.

questions.prompt: What is Marco's general attitude to big life changes?
options: They are hard, but worth trying if you really want them.
They are easy if you plan carefully.
People should never leave a safe job.
They are only possible for young people.
questions.explanation: Marco: *Don't expect it to be easy. But if you really want it, you should try.* Artinya sulit, tetapi layak dicoba.

speaking.title: Recent Changes in My Life
speaking.prompt: Talk for one to two minutes about how your life has changed recently. Mention at least three changes (for example: work, studies, home, hobbies, friends). Say how long each situation has lasted and when it started.
speaking.sampleAnswer: A lot has changed in my life recently. Last year I graduated from university, and in March I started my first full-time job at a design company. I've worked there for seven months now, and I've already learned a lot. I've also moved house. I used to live with my parents, but since August I've had my own small flat near the office. I haven't bought all the furniture yet, but it already feels like home. Finally, I've just joined a badminton club, so I play twice a week now.
tips: Pakai past simple untuk waktu yang selesai (last year, in March) dan present perfect untuk situasi yang masih berlangsung (for / since).
Use just / already / yet to sound natural when you talk about recent news.

speaking.title: A Story About an Unexpected Event
speaking.prompt: Tell a story about a day when something unexpected happened to you or someone you know. Describe the background, the main events in order, and how you felt at the end.
targetPhrases: It was raining / I was walking ...
speaking.sampleAnswer: It was a hot Saturday afternoon, and I was waiting for a bus in the city centre. I had just bought a birthday present for my sister. Suddenly, an old woman next to me fell and dropped her shopping. I helped her to sit down and called her son. By the time he arrived, a café owner had brought her a glass of water. I had never done anything like that before, and I felt nervous, but in the end the woman was fine. Her son was so grateful that he invited me to his restaurant for dinner.
tips: Use the past continuous for the background, the past simple for the main events, and the past perfect for things that happened earlier.
Gunakan kata penghubung seperti suddenly, luckily, after that, in the end agar ceritamu runtut.

speaking.title: If I Won a Big Prize
speaking.prompt: Imagine you have won a prize of 100,000 dollars. What would you do with the money? Would your life change? Also say one thing you wish were different in your life right now.
targetPhrases: I wish I had / were / could ...
speaking.sampleAnswer: If I won 100,000 dollars, I would first pay for my parents' house repairs, because the roof is very old. Then I'd probably save half of the money. I wouldn't buy an expensive car, because I don't really need one. If I had some money left, I could travel to South America; I've always wanted to see the mountains there. To be honest, my life wouldn't change very much. Right now, I wish I had more free time, because I work six days a week.
tips: Second conditional: If + past simple, would / could + V1. Ingat: If I were ..., bukan If I am ...
I wish + past simple untuk keinginan tentang masa sekarang: I wish I had more time.

speaking.title: Asking About Rules at a New Job
speaking.prompt: Role-play: It's your first day at a new job in a hotel. Ask your manager at least four questions about the rules (uniform, breaks, phones, working hours). Then repeat the rules back to check you understood.
speaking.sampleAnswer: Good morning! I have a few questions about the rules. Do I have to wear a uniform every day? And am I allowed to use my phone during my shift? Do I need to bring my own lunch, or is there a staff canteen? What time do I have to arrive on Saturdays? ... OK, so I have to wear the uniform, but I don't have to bring lunch because there's a canteen. And I mustn't use my phone at reception. Thank you, that's very clear.
tips: Bedakan mustn't (dilarang) dan don't have to (tidak wajib) saat mengulang aturan.
Use polite question forms: Do I have to ...? / Am I allowed to ...?

speaking.title: Passing On a Message
speaking.prompt: Role-play: Your colleague Siska phoned while your manager was out. Siska said: "I'm stuck in traffic. I'll be thirty minutes late. Can you start the meeting without me? I've sent the report by email." Now tell your manager what Siska said and what she asked.
speaking.sampleAnswer: Siska called about ten minutes ago. She said that she was stuck in traffic and that she would be thirty minutes late. She asked if we could start the meeting without her. She also told me that she had sent the report by email, so it should be in your inbox.
tips: Gunakan backshift: am → was, will → would, can → could, have sent → had sent.
Ingat: say something, tell someone something. Untuk pertanyaan: She asked if / whether ...

speaking.title: Life in Twenty Years
speaking.prompt: Give your predictions about daily life in twenty years. Talk about transport, work and technology at home. Say which predictions you are sure about and which are only possible.
speaking.sampleAnswer: I think daily life will be very different in twenty years. Cars will probably drive themselves, so people might not need a driving licence. More people will definitely work from home, and offices may become smaller. At home, I think robots will do some of the cleaning, but I don't think they'll cook as well as my mother! When electric cars become cheaper, our cities will be much quieter and cleaner.
tips: Will + probably/definitely untuk prediksi yang cukup yakin; might / may untuk kemungkinan.
After when / as soon as, use the present simple: When cars become cheaper ...

speaking.title: Pronouncing Contractions: I'd, You'd, Wouldn't
speaking.prompt: Read these sentences aloud three times. Focus on the short forms: 'd /d/, wouldn't /ˈwʊdnt/ and you'd better /juːd ˈbetə/. 1) If I were you, I'd call her. 2) You'd better not be late. 3) I wouldn't buy it if I were you. 4) We'd love to come.
speaking.sampleAnswer: If I were you, I'd call her. You'd better not be late. I wouldn't buy it if I were you. We'd love to come.
tips: Bunyi 'd sangat pendek, hampir tidak terdengar: I'd /aɪd/, we'd /wiːd/. Jangan ucapkan 'I would' terlalu jelas dalam percakapan santai.

speaking.title: Pronouncing Used To and -ed Endings
speaking.prompt: Read these sentences aloud. Pay attention to used to /ˈjuːs tə/ and the past participle endings /t/, /d/ and /ɪd/. 1) I used to live in a village. 2) She's worked here since May. 3) They've moved to Lakemoor. 4) We've decided to stay.
speaking.sampleAnswer: I used to live in a village. She's worked here since May. They've moved to Lakemoor. We've decided to stay.
tips: Used to diucapkan /ˈjuːs tə/ dengan bunyi /s/, bukan /z/, dan 'to' diucapkan lemah /tə/.
-ed is pronounced /ɪd/ only after /t/ or /d/ (decided, wanted). After other sounds, it is /t/ or /d/ (worked, moved).

writing.title: Email to a Friend: My News
writing.instructions: You haven't written to your friend Joko for six months. Write an informal email telling him your news. Include: (1) something important that has happened recently, (2) something you haven't done yet but plan to do, (3) a question about his life. Use the present perfect and the past simple correctly.
writing.modelAnswer:
Hi Joko,

Sorry I haven't written for so long! A lot has happened since my last email. The biggest news is that I've changed jobs. In July I left the bank and started working for a small travel company. I've been there for three months now, and I love it. I've already visited two new cities for work!

I haven't found a new flat yet, so I'm still living with my brother, but I'm going to look for one next month.

How about you? Have you finished your course? And how is your new puppy?

Write soon,
Ari

writing.title: Formal Email: A Problem with an Order
writing.instructions: You ordered a coffee machine online from a shop called HomeBright, but it arrived damaged. Write a formal email to customer service. Explain when you ordered it and when it was delivered, describe the problem, and say what you would like them to do. Use at least two passive sentences.
writing.modelAnswer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a coffee machine that I ordered from your website on 3 May (order number 45872).

The machine was delivered yesterday, but when I opened the box, I saw that the glass jug was broken and the side of the machine was badly scratched. The box was not damaged, so I believe the machine was packed carelessly.

I have attached two photos of the damage. I would be grateful if you could send me a replacement as soon as possible. If this is not possible, I would like a full refund.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Laras Wibowo

writing.title: Opinion: A Car-Free City Centre
writing.instructions: Your town council is considering a plan to ban cars from the city centre. Write your opinion for the council's website. Give at least two reasons and one possible problem. Use first conditional sentences (If ..., ... will ...) and unless / as long as at least once.
writing.modelAnswer:
In my opinion, banning cars from the city centre is a good idea, as long as the council improves public transport first.

Firstly, if there are no cars in the centre, the air will be much cleaner. Many children walk to school along the main street, and they breathe in polluted air every day. Secondly, if the streets are quieter, people will spend more time in the centre. Cafés and shops will probably get more customers.

However, there is one possible problem. Older people and people with disabilities will find it difficult to reach the centre unless there are enough buses and parking areas nearby.

To sum up, I support the plan, but the council must think carefully about people who can't walk long distances.

writing.title: A Story: The Day Everything Went Wrong
writing.instructions: Write a short story that begins with this sentence: 'It was supposed to be a perfect day.' Use the past continuous for background, the past simple for the main events, and the past perfect at least twice. Finish with how the day ended.
writing.modelAnswer: It was supposed to be a perfect day. The sun was shining and the birds were singing when I left home for my best friend's wedding. Unfortunately, I had forgotten to check the train times, and when I arrived at the station, my train had just left. I took a taxi, but halfway there it started to rain heavily and we got stuck in traffic. By the time I reached the hall, the ceremony had already started. I was wet, embarrassed and very late. I quietly sat down at the back. Then my friend turned around, saw me and smiled. After the ceremony she hugged me and said, 'You're here — that's what matters.' In the end, it was a perfect day after all.

writing.title: Summary: The Repair Café
writing.instructions: Read the article 'Fix It, Don't Throw It Away' in the Reading section. Write a summary of the main points in your own words. Include who started the café, what happens there, and why it is useful. Do not copy whole sentences from the article.
writing.modelAnswer: The Millbrook Repair Café was started three years ago by a retired engineer called Helen Marsh. Once a month, volunteers fix broken items such as lamps, clothes and laptops for free. Visitors watch the repairs so that they can learn to do them themselves. The café is useful because it saves people money and stops a lot of things from becoming waste. About 1,500 items have been repaired so far, and Helen hopes other towns will start similar cafés.

writing.title: Correct the Paragraph
writing.instructions:
The paragraph below has six mistakes (verb patterns, used to, passive and reported speech). Rewrite it correctly.

One day my teacher said me that the factory was closing. I asked her why was it closing, but she didn't know. Now I'm used to live in the city, but I still miss that smell.'
writing.modelAnswer: When I was a child, I used to live near a big factory. Chocolate was made there, and the whole street smelled sweet. I enjoyed watching the lorries arrive every morning. One day my teacher told me that the factory was closing. I asked her why it was closing, but she didn't know. Now I'm used to living in the city, but I still miss that smell.

vocabulary.definition: full of people

examples.id: Pasar itu selalu ramai pada Sabtu pagi.

vocabulary.definition: quiet and calm
